commands.result_summary:
1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)](#project-structure-from-uip-maestro-flow-init)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
44	
45	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
46	
47	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by `uip maestro flow init` and packaging. Do not add them manually.
48	
49	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
50	
51	## Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)
52	
53	```
54	<ProjectName>/
55	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
56	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
57	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
58	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
59	├── operate.json            # runtime options
60	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
61	```
62	
63	## Node instance
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "id": "rollDice",
68	  "type": "core.action.script",
69	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
70	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
71	  "inputs": {
72	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
73	  },
74	  "outputs": {
75	    "output": {
76	      "type": "object",
77	      "description": "The return value of the script",
78	      "source": "=result.response",
79	      "var": "output"
80	    },
81	    "error": {
82	      "type": "object",
83	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
84	      "source": "=result.Error",
85	      "var": "error"
86	    }
87	  }
88	}
89	```
90	
91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
106	
107	### Instance-specific identity fields
108	
109	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
110	
111	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
112	|-------|---------|---------|
113	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
114	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
115	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
116	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
117	
118	Example — manual start trigger:
119	
120	```json
121	{
122	  "id": "start",
123	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
124	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
125	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
126	  "inputs": {
127	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
128	  },
129	  "outputs": {
130	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "The return value of the trigger.", "source": "=result.response", "var": "output" }
131	  }
132	}
133	```
134	
135	### Node outputs
136	
137	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
138	
139	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
140	
141	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
142	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
143	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
144	
145	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
146	
147	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
148	
149	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
150	- `description` — human-readable description
151	- `source` — runtime binding expression (e.g., `"=result.response"` for the primary output, `"=result.Error"` for errors)
152	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
153	
154	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector, agent):
155	
156	```json
157	"outputs": {
158	  "output": {
159	    "type": "object",
160	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
161	    "source": "=result.response",
162	    "var": "output"
163	  },
164	  "error": {
165	    "type": "object",
166	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
167	    "source": "=result.Error",
168	    "var": "error"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port:
174	
175	```json
176	"outputs": {
177	  "output": {
178	    "type": "object",
179	    "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
180	    "source": "=result.response",
181	    "var": "output"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
187	
188	## Layout
189	
190	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
191	
192	```json
193	"layout": {
194	  "nodes": {
195	    "start": {
196	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
197	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
198	      "collapsed": false
199	    },
200	    "rollDice": {
201	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
202	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
203	      "collapsed": false
204	    },
205	    "end": {
206	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
207	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
208	      "collapsed": false
209	    }
210	  }
211	}
212	```
213	
214	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
215	
216	**What format does:**
217	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
218	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
219	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
220	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
221	
222	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
223	
224	## Edge — both ports required
225	
226	```json
227	{
228	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
229	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
230	  "sourcePort": "output",
231	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
232	  "targetPort": "input"
233	}
234	```
235	
236	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
237	>
238	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
239	
240	## Definition entry
241	
242	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
243	
244	```bash
245	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
246	```
247	
248	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array. Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.
249	
250	## Common node types
251	
252	| Type | Purpose | Key inputs |
253	|------|---------|------------|
254	| `core.trigger.manual` | Entry point | `entryPointId` |
255	| `core.trigger.scheduled` | Recurring schedule trigger | `entryPointId`, `timerType`, `timerPreset` |
256	| `core.action.script` | Run JavaScript | `script` |
257	| `core.action.http.v2` | HTTP request | `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body` |
258	| `core.action.transform` | Map/filter/group data | `collection`, `operations` |
259	| `core.logic.decision` | If/else branch | `expression` |
260	| `core.logic.switch` | Multi-way branch | `cases` |
261	| `core.logic.loop` | Iterate collection | `collection`, `parallel` |
262	| `core.logic.merge` | Sync parallel paths | — |
263	| `core.control.end` | Graceful end | — |
264	| `core.logic.terminate` | Abort workflow | — |
265	
266	> The BPMN type for each node (e.g., `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`) lives in the `definitions` entry copied from `uip maestro flow registry get`. Instances do not carry the BPMN type.
267	
268	For full details on each node (ports, inputs, outputs, when to use), see the [Author planning architecture guide](../author/references/planning-arch.md). For implementation resolution (registry lookups, connection binding, reference field resolution), see the [Author planning implementation guide](../author/references/planning-impl.md).
269	
270	Discover all available types:
271	```bash
272	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
273	uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>
274	```
275	
276	## Standard ports by node type
277	
278	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
279	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
280	| `core.trigger.manual` | `output` | — |
281	| `core.action.script` | `success`, `error` | `input` |
282	| `core.action.http.v2` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic) | `input` |
283	| `core.action.transform` | `output`, `error` | `input` |
284	| `core.logic.decision` | `true`, `false` | `input` |
285	| `core.logic.switch` | `case-{id}` (dynamic), `default` | `input` |
286	| `core.logic.loop` | `success`, `output` | `input`, `loopBack` |
287	| `core.logic.merge` | `output` | `input` |
288	| `core.control.end` | — | `input` |
289	| `core.logic.terminate` | — | `input` |
290	
291	Connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes follow the same pattern as the generic action nodes above: a primary source port plus an implicit `error` port.
292	
293	Verify exact ports for any node type:
294	```bash
295	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
296	# Look at Data.Node.handleConfiguration[].handles[].id
297	# Also check Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling — see "Implicit error port" below
298	```
299	
300	## Implicit error port on action nodes
301	
302	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
303	
304	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
305	
306	### When the error port fires
307	
308	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
309	- Request timeouts
310	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
311	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
312	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
313	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
314	
315	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`.
316	
317	### Wiring the error port
318	
319	```bash
320	# Confirm the node supports error handling
321	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
322	
323	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
324	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
325	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
326	```
327	
328	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself:
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
333	  "inputs": {
334	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
335	  }
336	}
337	```
338	
339	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
340	
341	### Error port vs other branching
342	
343	| Mechanism | When to use |
344	| --- | --- |
345	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
346	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
347	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
348	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |
349	
350	## Minimal working example — dice roller
351	
352	Building a flow is a two-step process: write the nodes/edges structure, then populate `definitions` from the registry.
353	
354	### Step 1 — Write nodes and edges
355	
356	Replace `<uuid>` with any generated UUID (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` in Node.js, or any UUID v4 generator). The same UUID must appear in `entry-points.json` as `uniqueId`. Set top-level `version` to the value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds — never hand-pick it (see [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)).
357	
358	```json
359	{
360	  "id": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5",
361	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
362	  "name": "DiceRoller",
363	  "nodes": [
364	    {
365	      "id": "start",
366	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
367	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
368	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
369	      "inputs": {
370	        "entryPointId": "<uuid>"
371	      },
372	      "outputs": {
373	        "output": {
374	          "type": "object",
375	          "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
376	          "source": "=result.response",
377	          "var": "output"
378	        }
379	      }
380	    },
381	    {
382	      "id": "rollDice",
383	      "type": "core.action.script",
384	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
385	      "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
386	      "inputs": {
387	        "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
388	      },
389	      "outputs": {
390	        "output": {
391	          "type": "object",
392	          "description": "The return value of the script",
393	          "source": "=result.response",
394	          "var": "output"
395	        },
396	        "error": {
397	          "type": "object",
398	          "description": "Error information if the script fails",
399	          "source": "=result.Error",
400	          "var": "error"
401	        }
402	      }
403	    },
404	    {
405	      "id": "end",
406	      "type": "core.logic.terminate",
407	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
408	      "display": { "label": "End" },
409	      "inputs": {}
410	    }
411	  ],
412	  "edges": [
413	    {
414	      "id": "edge-start-roll",
415	      "sourceNodeId": "start",
416	      "sourcePort": "output",
417	      "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
418	      "targetPort": "input"
419	    },
420	    {
421	      "id": "edge-roll-end",
422	      "sourceNodeId": "rollDice",
423	      "sourcePort": "success",
424	      "targetNodeId": "end",
425	      "targetPort": "input"
426	    }
427	  ],
428	  "definitions": [],
429	  "bindings": [],
430	  "variables": {},
431	  "layout": {
432	    "nodes": {
433	      "start": {
434	        "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
435	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
436	        "collapsed": false
437	      },
438	      "rollDice": {
439	        "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
440	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
441	        "collapsed": false
442	      },
443	      "end": {
444	        "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
445	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
446	        "collapsed": false
447	      }
448	    }
449	  }
450	}
451	```
452	
453	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
454	
455	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
456	
457	```bash
458	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
459	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
460	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
461	```
462	
463	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
464	
465	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
466	
467	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
468	
469	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). **Do not edit this file directly** — it is auto-generated by `uip maestro flow init` and regenerated by `uip maestro flow debug` before upload. Manual edits will be overwritten.
470	
471	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
472	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
473	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
474	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
475	
476	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
477	
478	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
479	
480	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
481	
482	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
483	
484	```json
485	"bindings": [
486	  {
487	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
488	    "name": "name",
489	    "type": "string",
490	    "resource": "process",
491	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
492	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
493	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
494	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
495	  },
496	  {
497	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
498	    "name": "folderPath",
499	    "type": "string",
500	    "resource": "process",
501	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
502	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
503	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
504	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
505	  }
506	]
507	```
508	
509	**Rules:**
510	
511	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
512	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
513	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
514	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
515	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
516	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
517	
518	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
519	
520	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
521	
522	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
523	
524	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
525	
526	## Bindings — connector connection binding
527	
528	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
529	
530	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.

1	# Connector Trigger Nodes — Implementation
2	
3	How to configure connector trigger nodes: connection binding, enriched metadata, event parameter resolution, and trigger-specific `node configure` fields. This replaces the IS activity workflow (Steps 1-6 in [connector/impl.md](../connector/impl.md)) — trigger nodes have different metadata and configuration.
4	
5	> **This plugin covers two node families that share the same configuration mechanism:**
6	>
7	> - **Connector triggers** (`uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>`) — start node; the event starts the flow. The default subject of every step below.
8	> - **Wait for events** (`uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>`) — a mid-flow event node; the flow pauses and waits for the event before continuing. Same connection binding, enriched metadata, event parameter resolution, filter trees, and `node configure` fields. Only the placement and node lifecycle differ. See [Wait for events](#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent) for the deltas, then apply Steps 1-6 below unchanged.
9	
10	## Configuration Workflow
11	
12	Follow these steps for every IS trigger node.
13	
14	### Step 1 — Fetch a preliminary connection and query trigger objects
15	
16	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.trigger.<connector-key>.<trigger-name>`) and the operation name from the `registry get` response (`model.context[].operation`).
17	
18	**1a. Get any enabled connection** — needed as `--connection-id` for `triggers objects` below.
19	
20	Discovery call is **always**:
21	
22	```bash
23	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
24	```
25	
26	`--all-folders` is mandatory. Without it the CLI returns the active folder only and hides connections in other folders the user can see. Plain `uip is connections list "<connector-key>"` is forbidden for discovery.
27	
28	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md). Single source of truth for selection rules, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, ping verification.
29	
30	Pick any enabled connection (prefer `IsDefault: Yes`) and capture its `Id` for Step 1b.
31	
32	**1b. Query trigger objects** — **mandatory** for every trigger node. Do NOT skip:
33	
34	```bash
35	uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
36	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
37	```
38	
39	Save the response. It carries three pieces per event object that drive later steps:
40	
41	| Field | Drives | Meaning |
42	|------|--------|---------|
43	| `byoaConnection` | Step 1c | If `true`, only BYOA connections are valid for this event |
44	| `isWebhookUrlVisible` | Step 6b | If `true`, retrieve and present the webhook URL |
45	| **`parameters[]`** | Steps 3 & 4 | Object-, query-, and path-scoped input parameters (e.g. shared mailbox, repo, owner). **NOT the complete event-parameter set** — merge with `EventParameters` from `triggers describe` (Step 1b-2). The full input set is the **union** of both; a field is required if either source marks it `required`. |
46	
47	It may also include `design.textBlocks` with connector-specific user-facing instructions (e.g., "Add this URL to your Slack app's Event Subscriptions"). Surface that text verbatim when applicable — do not invent service-specific guidance.
48	
49	> `byoaConnection` and `isWebhookUrlVisible` are per event object, not per connector — some connectors require BYOA for some events but not others. `parameters[]` is per event object too: each operation has its own input fields.
50	
51	#### Reading `parameters[]`
52	
53	Each entry is one input field the user supplies when configuring the trigger (e.g., GitHub `repo`, Outlook `parentFolderId`, Slack `channelId`). For each:
54	
55	| Key | Use |
56	|---|---|
57	| `name` | Key inside the `--detail` bucket selected by `type` — see below |
58	| `displayName` | Label when prompting the user for a missing value |
59	| `dataType` | Value type (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, …) |
60	| `required` | Drives Step 4's required-field check |

content_blocks.text:
Good question! There are several great automatic trigger options available on your tenant, and the right one depends on how your vendors actually send invoices. Let me ask so I can wire the right one:

**How do vendor invoices arrive?** Pick the option that matches your setup:

1. **Outlook 365 email** — invoices arrive as email attachments in an Outlook/Microsoft 365 mailbox → triggers the moment a new email lands
2. **Gmail** — invoices arrive as email attachments in a Gmail inbox → triggers on every new email received
3. **Generic email (IMAP/POP3)** — invoices arrive via another mail server → triggers on email received
4. **OneDrive / SharePoint folder** — vendors upload invoice PDFs to a shared OneDrive or SharePoint folder → triggers when a new file appears
5. **Google Drive folder** — invoices land in a shared Google Drive folder → triggers on new file created
6. **Scheduled (poll on a timer)** — run the flow every N minutes/hours to pick up new invoices (no external connection needed — works with any source you can query)
7. **Something else** — e.g., Box, Dropbox, a webhook, or another system

> **Tip:** Options 1–3 are the most common for vendor invoices (vendors email PDFs). Options 4–5 work great if your AP team has a shared drive where invoices are dropped. Option 6 is the simplest to set up since it requires no connector configuration.

commands.result_summary:
1	# Connector Trigger Nodes — Implementation
2	
3	How to configure connector trigger nodes: connection binding, enriched metadata, event parameter resolution, and trigger-specific `node configure` fields. This replaces the IS activity workflow (Steps 1-6 in [connector/impl.md](../connector/impl.md)) — trigger nodes have different metadata and configuration.
4	
5	> **This plugin covers two node families that share the same configuration mechanism:**
6	>
7	> - **Connector triggers** (`uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>`) — start node; the event starts the flow. The default subject of every step below.
8	> - **Wait for events** (`uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>`) — a mid-flow event node; the flow pauses and waits for the event before continuing. Same connection binding, enriched metadata, event parameter resolution, filter trees, and `node configure` fields. Only the placement and node lifecycle differ. See [Wait for events](#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent) for the deltas, then apply Steps 1-6 below unchanged.
9	
10	## Configuration Workflow
11	
12	Follow these steps for every IS trigger node.
13	
14	### Step 1 — Fetch a preliminary connection and query trigger objects
15	
16	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.trigger.<connector-key>.<trigger-name>`) and the operation name from the `registry get` response (`model.context[].operation`).
17	
18	**1a. Get any enabled connection** — needed as `--connection-id` for `triggers objects` below.
19	
20	Discovery call is **always**:
21	
22	```bash
23	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
24	```
25	
26	`--all-folders` is mandatory. Without it the CLI returns the active folder only and hides connections in other folders the user can see. Plain `uip is connections list "<connector-key>"` is forbidden for discovery.
27	
28	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md). Single source of truth for selection rules, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, ping verification.
29	
30	Pick any enabled connection (prefer `IsDefault: Yes`) and capture its `Id` for Step 1b.
31	
32	**1b. Query trigger objects** — **mandatory** for every trigger node. Do NOT skip:
33	
34	```bash
35	uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
36	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
37	```
38	
39	Save the response. It carries three pieces per event object that drive later steps:
40	
41	| Field | Drives | Meaning |
42	|------|--------|---------|
43	| `byoaConnection` | Step 1c | If `true`, only BYOA connections are valid for this event |
44	| `isWebhookUrlVisible` | Step 6b | If `true`, retrieve and present the webhook URL |
45	| **`parameters[]`** | Steps 3 & 4 | Object-, query-, and path-scoped input parameters (e.g. shared mailbox, repo, owner). **NOT the complete event-parameter set** — merge with `EventParameters` from `triggers describe` (Step 1b-2). The full input set is the **union** of both; a field is required if either source marks it `required`. |
46	
47	It may also include `design.textBlocks` with connector-specific user-facing instructions (e.g., "Add this URL to your Slack app's Event Subscriptions"). Surface that text verbatim when applicable — do not invent service-specific guidance.
48	
49	> `byoaConnection` and `isWebhookUrlVisible` are per event object, not per connector — some connectors require BYOA for some events but not others. `parameters[]` is per event object too: each operation has its own input fields.
50	
51	#### Reading `parameters[]`
52	
53	Each entry is one input field the user supplies when configuring the trigger (e.g., GitHub `repo`, Outlook `parentFolderId`, Slack `channelId`). For each:
54	
55	| Key | Use |
56	|---|---|
57	| `name` | Key inside the `--detail` bucket selected by `type` — see below |
58	| `displayName` | Label when prompting the user for a missing value |
59	| `dataType` | Value type (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, …) |
60	| `required` | Drives Step 4's required-field check |
61	| `reference` | Present → resolve to an ID in Step 3 (`uip is resources run list`) before configure |
62	| `description` | Field hint — surface verbatim when prompting |
63	| `design.position` | `"primary"` indicates a top-level input field; other positions are layout hints — safe to ignore for configure |
64	| `type` | Bucket selector in Step 6's `--detail`: `"query"` → `queryParameters`, `"path"` → `pathParameters`, else → `eventParameters` |
65	
66	> **Source of truth — the UNION of two calls, never one alone.** The complete event-input set = `triggers objects → parameters[]` (object/query/path scope) **∪** `triggers describe → EventParameters` (event-config scope). Configure every field that **either** marks `required: true`. `triggers describe → FilterFields` feeds the `filter` tree; `OutputFields` / `outputResponseDefinition` feed downstream `$vars`. `flow registry get`'s `eventParameters.fields` mirrors `describe` and is the offline fallback. A required field can appear in `describe → EventParameters` while absent from `parameters[]`, so **both calls are mandatory and you must merge them**. Full field semantics: [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md — `parameters[]`](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#parameters--event-parameter-input-fields).
67	
68	**1b-2. Resolve the object name and fetch field metadata** — **mandatory** for every trigger node.
69	
70	> **MUST READ before this step:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md). Single source of truth for fetching trigger parameters and fields — object name resolution, describe call, source-of-truth contract.
71	
72	1. Resolve `<objectName>` from the Step 1b `triggers objects` response per [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md — Object Name Resolution](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#object-name-resolution). If the object name is not recognizable from the user's prompt, **ask the user** — present candidates by `displayName`. Do NOT guess.
73	2. Fetch field metadata:
74	
75	```bash
76	uip is triggers describe "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" "<objectName>" \
77	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
78	```
79	
80	> **Source of truth for node configuration — merge both responses.** Event-parameter inputs = the **union** of `triggers objects → parameters[]` (Step 1b) and `triggers describe → EventParameters` (this step). `triggers describe` also returns `FilterFields` (→ `filter` tree) and `OutputFields` (→ downstream `$vars`). Never treat `triggers describe` as "only field metadata" — its `EventParameters` are first-class event parameters and frequently carry required fields that `parameters[]` omits. Do NOT skip this call, and do NOT invent parameters or fields.
81	
82	### Step 1c — Select the final connection
83	
84	**If `byoaConnection: true`** — the Step 1a connection is not usable. Follow the BYOA selection workflow in [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md — For BYOA Connections](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md#for-byoa-connections-webhook-triggers) (filter with `--byoa`, `--refresh` retry, stop-and-ask if none exist).
85	
86	**If `byoaConnection: false`** — use the Step 1a connection. Verify health:
87	
88	```bash
89	uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json
90	```
91	
92	### Step 2 — Get enriched trigger metadata
93	
94	`--connection-id` is **required** for trigger nodes. Without it, the command fails.
95	
96	```bash
97	uip maestro flow registry get <trigger-node-type> --connection-id <connection-id> --output json
98	```
99	
100	The response contains three trigger-specific sections:
101	
102	**`eventParameters.fields`** — non-authoritative. Often empty (see Step 1b). Iterate [`parameters[]`](#reading-parameters) from Step 1b in Steps 3 and 4 — do not iterate this block.
103	
104	Shape only — do not iterate:
105	
106	```json
107	{
108	  "eventParameters": {
109	    "fields": [
110	      {
111	        "name": "parentFolderId",
112	        "displayName": "Email folder",
113	        "type": "string",
114	        "required": true,
115	        "reference": {
116	          "objectName": "MailFolder",
117	          "lookupValue": "id",
118	          "lookupNames": ["displayName"],
119	          "path": "/MailFolders"
120	        }
121	      }
122	    ]
123	  }
124	}
125	```
126	
127	**`filterFields`** — fields used to narrow *which* events fire the trigger (e.g., only emails from a specific sender). These are optional filter criteria and are passed as a structured tree in `--detail.filter` (see [Filter Trees](#filter-trees)).
128	
129	```json
130	{
131	  "filterFields": {
132	    "fields": [
133	      {
134	        "name": "fromAddress",
135	        "displayName": "From address",
136	        "type": "string",
137	        "required": false
138	      }
139	    ]
140	  }
141	}
142	```
143	
144	**`outputResponseDefinition`** — the event payload schema (all fields the trigger outputs when it fires). **Save this** — you need it in Step 4b to know the exact field paths for downstream `$vars` expressions (e.g., `$vars.{nodeId}.output.text`, `$vars.{nodeId}.output.channel`). Do not guess output field names.
145	
146	**`eventMode`** — `"webhooks"` or `"polling"`.
147	
148	The response (which becomes the `definitions[]` entry verbatim) includes `model.context` with:
149	- `connectorKey` — the connector identifier
150	- `operation` — the event operation name (e.g., `"EMAIL_RECEIVED"`, `"ISSUE_CREATED"`)
151	- `objectName` — the IS object (e.g., `"Message"`, `"Issue"`)
152	
153	These live in the **definition**, not on the node instance. The instance carries only `inputs` (event filter fields) and `outputs`.
154	
155	### Step 3 — Resolve reference fields in event parameters
156	
157	Iterate the **union** of `parameters[]` (Step 1b) and `EventParameters` (Step 1b-2). For each entry with a `reference` key, run an ID lookup — same mechanism as IS activity nodes. A referenced field can live in `describe → EventParameters` while absent from `parameters[]` — resolving only `parameters[]` misses it.
158	
159	> **Resolve every reference field freshly, against the current `--connection-id`, immediately before `node configure` (Step 6)** — even if you think you already know the ID from a previous flow. Reference IDs are connection-scoped and reused values fault silently at runtime. See [Reference IDs Are Connection-Scoped (CRITICAL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical) for the full mechanism and failure mode, and the top-level Anti-Patterns in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
160	
161	```bash
162	# Example: resolve Outlook mail folder "Inbox" to its ID
163	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<reference.objectName>" \
164	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
165	```
166	
167	The `<id>` in `--connection-id "<id>"` MUST be the connection bound to **this** flow (the final connection from Step 1c), not any other connection you've used in another flow. Use the resolved IDs — from this very `run list` call — in the trigger's event parameter configuration.
168	
169	> **Paginate when looking up by name.** Use `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` with `--query "nextPage=<token>"`. Short-circuit on match. Do NOT conclude "not found" until `HasMore` is `"false"`. See [resources.md#pagination](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md#pagination).
170	
171	**Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — Integration Service — resources.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) for the full reference-resolution workflow** (pagination, describe failures, fallbacks).
172	
173	### Step 4 — Validate required event parameters
174	
175	Check every entry in the **union** of `parameters[]` (Step 1b) and `EventParameters` (Step 1b-2). Treat a field as required if **either** source marks `required: true`. All required event parameters must have values before building the flow.
176	
177	1. Collect all required entries from `parameters[]` **and** `describe → EventParameters` (dedupe by `name`); required = required in either
178	2. For each, check if the user's prompt provides a value
179	3. If any required field is missing, **ask the user** — list the missing fields with their `displayName` (and `description` if useful). Free-form input is appropriate when the value space is open-ended; when a finite set of sensible values exists, present them as options per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
180	4. Only proceed after all required event parameters are resolved
181	
182	> Step 6 buckets each resolved value into `eventParameters`, `queryParameters`, or `pathParameters` based on the entry's `type` — see Step 6's `--detail` table.
183	
184	### Step 4b — Map trigger output fields for downstream nodes
185	
186	Before wiring downstream nodes, check `outputResponseDefinition` from Step 2 to know the exact field names available in `$vars.{triggerId}.output`. Do NOT guess field names — different triggers output different schemas.
187	
188	Each trigger type has a different output schema — field names like `.text`, `.subject`, or `.body.content` vary by connector. Use the actual field names from `outputResponseDefinition` when writing expressions in downstream nodes.
189	
190	### Step 5 — Replace the manual trigger with the connector trigger node
191	
192	Follow the [CLI: Replace manual trigger with connector trigger](../../editing-operations-cli.md#replace-manual-trigger-with-connector-trigger) procedure. The CLI handles edge cleanup, orphaned definition removal, and `variables.nodes` regeneration automatically. Note the generated node ID from the `node add` response — you need it for Step 6.
193	
194	### Step 6 — Configure the trigger node
195	
196	> **MUST READ before `node configure`:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md). The parameters fetched there (`triggers objects` → `parameters[]`, Step 1b) and fields (`triggers describe`, Step 1b-2) are the source of truth for everything in `--detail`. If you have not run both calls, go back to Step 1b.
197	
198	**Read the `--detail` field table below before calling `node configure`.** The fields and types are strict — unknown keys or wrong types cause validation errors. Do not guess field names from other node types (e.g., activity nodes use `method`/`endpoint`/`bodyParameters`; triggers use `eventMode`/`eventParameters`/`filter`, plus `objectName` for generic triggers).
199	
200	Use `node configure` with trigger-specific `--detail` fields:
201	
202	```bash
203	uip maestro flow node configure <PROJECT>.flow <triggerId> --output json --detail '{
204	  "connectionId": "<CONNECTION_ID>",
205	  "folderKey": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
206	  "eventMode": "<EVENT_MODE>",
207	  "objectName": "<OBJECT_NAME>",
208	  "eventParameters": { "<paramName>": "<RESOLVED_VALUE>" },
209	  "filter": {
210	    "groupOperator": 0,
211	    "index": 0,
212	    "filters": [
213	      {
214	        "id": "subject",
215	        "operator": "Contains",
216	        "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true }
217	      }
218	    ]
219	  }
220	}'
221	```
222	
223	**`--detail` fields for triggers:**
224	
225	| Field | Required | Description |
226	|---|---|---|
227	| `connectionId` | Yes | Connection UUID from Step 1c (the final connection — BYOA if required) |
228	| `folderKey` | Yes | Orchestrator folder key for the connection |
229	| `eventMode` | Yes | `"webhooks"` or `"polling"` — from `registry get` response |
230	| `objectName` | Generic triggers only | The IS object the event subscribes to (e.g. the Data Fabric entity name) — the object name resolved in Step 1b-2. **Required for generic triggers** (`activityType: "GenericTrigger"` in the definition's `connectorDetail.configuration` — one manifest templated across every object, so its `objectName` context entry ships empty). **Omit for curated triggers** (`activityType: "CuratedTrigger"`) — the manifest's baked-in objectName always wins. |
231	| `eventParameters`, `queryParameters`, `pathParameters` | No | JSON objects of resolved values from Steps 3-4. Bucket each `parameters[]` entry by its `type`: `"query"` → `queryParameters` (e.g. GitHub `{"repo":"cli"}`, Outlook `{"sharedMailboxAddress":"..."}`), `"path"` → `pathParameters` (e.g. GitHub `{"owner":"uipath"}`), otherwise → `eventParameters`. Within each bucket, the key is `parameters[].name`. Each must be a JSON object. |
232	| `filter` | No | Structured filter tree — see [Filter Trees](#filter-trees) below. Omit to trigger on all events |
233	
234	The CLI computes the runtime JMESPath `filterExpression` from `filter` automatically and persists both into the workflow so Studio Web can re-open the trigger without losing the filter configuration. **Do not pass `filterExpression` directly — the validator rejects it.**
235	The command populates `inputs.detail` (including the internal `configuration` blob with the `filter` tree and combined `filterExpression`) and creates workflow-level connection bindings.
236	
237	> **Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file: `uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json`

239	### Step 6b — Retrieve and display webhook URL (webhooks only)
240	
241	Applies when `eventMode` is `"webhooks"`, regardless of `byoaConnection`.
242	
243	> **Guard:** If the trigger object's `isWebhookUrlVisible` is `false` (from Step 1b), skip this step — the connector manages webhook registration automatically and does not expose a URL. If you do not have `triggers objects` output, you skipped Step 1b — go back.
244	
245	Follow [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval) for the exact commands (`uip is connections list` → `ElementInstanceId` → `uip is webhooks config`).
246	
247	**Presenting the URL:** If the Step 1b `triggers objects` response included `design.textBlocks`, use that text verbatim (substituting `{webhookUrl}`) — it carries connector-specific registration instructions. Otherwise, use a generic message instructing the user to register the URL in their external service's app settings (e.g., Slack Event Subscriptions, Salesforce Outbound Messages). The trigger will not fire until the URL is registered and verified.

If `webhooks config` itself fails, ping the connection (`uip is connections ping`) and re-authenticate via `uip is connections edit` if unhealthy.

253	## Wait for events (`uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>`)
254	
255	A **Wait for events** node waits for an external event **mid-flow** instead of starting the flow ("wait for the approval reply", "wait until the Jira issue is Done"). Same connector event as a trigger — identical `eventParameters`, `filterFields`, `outputResponseDefinition`, `eventMode`, connection binding, reference resolution, filter trees. Apply Steps 1-6 above unchanged; only the deltas below differ.
256	
257	| Aspect | Connector **trigger** | **Wait for events** (mid-flow) |
258	|---|---|---|
259	| Node type | `uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>` | `uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>` |
260	| Position | Start node — replaces the manual trigger | Mid-flow — has an `input` port |
261	| Add | Step 5: [replace the manual trigger](../../editing-operations-cli.md#replace-manual-trigger-with-connector-trigger) | `node add` like an action node; do **NOT** remove the start node |
262	| Ports | in: — · out: `output` | in: `input` · out: `output`, `error` |
263	| Start trigger | Is the flow's trigger | Not a trigger — flow still needs its own start trigger |
264	| Discovery search | `... search "<svc>" trigger` | `... search "<svc>" event` |
265	| Config (Steps 1-4, 6) | Identical | Identical |
266	
267	Add and wire:
268	
269	```bash
270	uip maestro flow node add <PROJECT>.flow uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event> \
271	  --label "<LABEL>" --position 400,144 --output json
272	```
273	
274	Wire an incoming edge into `input` and an outgoing edge from `output` per [editing-operations-json.md — Insert a node between two existing nodes](../../editing-operations-json.md#insert-a-node-between-two-existing-nodes). Downstream reads `$vars.{eventNodeId}.output` (payload) and `$vars.{eventNodeId}.error`; wire `error` to survive an event-wait failure.
275	
276	> **The flow still needs a separate start trigger.** A mid-flow event node does **not** start the flow. Do not remove `core.trigger.manual`/`scheduled` or the connector trigger that begins the flow.

280	## Filter Trees
281	
282	Filters are authored as a **structured tree**, not a string expression. The CLI compiles the tree into a JMESPath `filterExpression` using the same logic Studio Web does, and writes both forms into the flow so the trigger round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
283	
284	### Tree shape
285	
286	```jsonc
287	{
288	  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
289	  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
290	  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
291	    {
292	      "id": "<fieldName>",        // from filterFields.fields[].name
293	      "operator": "<Operator>",   // see operator table below
294	      "value": {
295	        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time
296	        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
297	        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not supported
298	      }
299	    }
300	  ],
301	  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
302	}
303	```
304	
305	A no-op filter — used when the user wants all events to fire the trigger — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
306	
307	### Supported operators
308	
309	| Operator | Meaning | Typical field types |
310	|---|---|---|
311	| `Equals` / `NotEquals` | Exact (in)equality | string, number, boolean |
312	| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | Numeric comparison | number, integer |
313	| `Contains` / `NotContains` | Substring match | string |
314	| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | Prefix / suffix match | string |
315	| `IsEmpty` / `IsNotEmpty` | Value is / is not empty string | string (no `value` needed) |
316	| `Is` / `IsNot` | Boolean is true / false | boolean (no `value` needed) |
317	| `In` / `NotIn` / `IsOneOf` / `IsNotOneOf` | Membership — pass comma-separated values in `value.value` | string, number |
318	| `Before` / `BeforeOrEqual` / `After` / `AfterOrEqual` / `DateTimeEquals` / `DateTimeNotEqual` | Date-time comparison (ISO-8601 strings) | date-time |
319	
320	### Examples
321	
322	**Emails containing "urgent" in the subject:**
323	
324	```json
325	{
326	  "groupOperator": 0,
327	  "index": 0,
328	  "filters": [
329	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
330	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
331	  ]
332	}
333	```
334	
335	**Emails from a specific sender AND subject contains "good day":**
336	
337	```json
338	{
339	  "groupOperator": 0,
340	  "index": 0,
341	  "filters": [
342	    { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
343	      "value": { "value": "boss@example.com", "rawString": "\"boss@example.com\"", "isLiteral": true } },
344	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
345	      "value": { "value": "good day", "rawString": "\"good day\"", "isLiteral": true } }
346	  ]
347	}
348	```
349	
350	**Multiple senders (OR) nested inside an outer AND with a subject match:**
351	
352	```json
353	{
354	  "groupOperator": 0,
355	  "index": 0,
356	  "filters": [
357	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
358	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
359	  ],
360	  "groups": [
361	    {
362	      "groupOperator": 1,
363	      "index": 1,
364	      "filters": [
365	        { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
366	          "value": { "value": "a@ex.com", "rawString": "\"a@ex.com\"", "isLiteral": true } },
367	        { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
368	          "value": { "value": "b@ex.com", "rawString": "\"b@ex.com\"", "isLiteral": true } }
369	      ]
370	    }
371	  ]
372	}
373	```
374	
375	### How to build a filter tree from `filterFields`
376	
377	1. Run `flow registry get` with `--connection-id` (Step 2) and read the `filterFields.fields` array. Each entry has a `name` (use as the leaf `id`), a `type` (drives operator selection), and an optional `description`.
378	
379	Then follow [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md > Building Filter Trees from filterFields](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#building-filter-trees-from-filterfields) for the rest of the procedure (operator selection, leaf composition, value wrapping), the mandatory-filter contract (connector-mandated values like Gmail folder go on `eventParameters`, never the freeform `filter` tree), and array-shaped field handling.
380	
381	### What NOT to generate
382	
383	| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
384	|---|---|---|
385	| `"filterExpression": "(contains(subject, 'x'))"` | Legacy format — the CLI now rejects `filterExpression` as an input field (see MST-8802). It is *only* an output in the generated `.flow`. | Build a `filter` tree with a `Contains` leaf. |
386	| `"filter": "(subject == 'x')"` | `filter` must be an object, not a string. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
387	| `{ "id": "fields.subject", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `filterFields.fields[].name`. | `{ "id": "subject", ... }` |
388	| `{ "id": "subject", "operator": "contains", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive — use PascalCase. | `"operator": "Contains"` |
389	| `{ "value": "urgent" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
390	| `{ "isLiteral": false, "value": "${var}" }` | Expression values are not yet supported by the CLI port. | Resolve the value first, then pass it as a literal. |
391	| Adding a freeform leaf for a connector-mandated field (e.g. Gmail folder, Slack channelId) | Mandatory filters derived from connector event metadata are emitted automatically by the CLI from `eventParameters` — duplicating them in the freeform tree double-applies the clause. | Set the value through `eventParameters` only; the CLI AND-joins the mandatory JMES clause into the top-level `inputs.detail.filterExpression` (matching SW's `combinedFilterExpression`). It is *not* persisted on `essentialConfiguration` — SW classifies it optional and rebuilds it from input field values on restore. |

442	## Testing Trigger Flows
443	
444	`uip maestro flow debug` works with trigger-based flows. Debug does **not** wait for a live event — it **pulls the most recent matching event** from the connector's lookback window and executes immediately.
445	
446	### How debug works for triggers
447	
448	1. Debug calls the connector's `/events/debug` endpoint with `maxResults=5` and a `startDate` (default: 1 hour ago)
449	2. The connector returns up to 5 matching events from that window, sorted most-recent-first
450	3. The runtime uses `FilterMatches[0]` (the most recent match) as the trigger input
451	4. The flow executes immediately with that event data
452	5. If **no matching events** exist in the lookback window, debug fails with error code `3005` (TriggerNoMatches)
453	
454	```bash
455	uip maestro flow debug . --output json
456	# → Fetches most recent matching event from the past ~1 hour
457	# → Flow executes immediately with that event data
458	```
459	
460	### Polling vs webhook triggers in debug
461	
462	| Trigger mode | Debug support | Behavior |
463	|---|---|---|
464	| `polling` | Supported | Pulls recent events via debug API, executes immediately |
465	| `webhooks` | **Not supported** | Webhook triggers cannot be tested in Studio debug mode — debug requires Orchestrator |
466	
467	> **If the trigger uses `webhooks` event mode**, tell the user that debug is not available for webhook triggers. They must deploy to Orchestrator and test with a real webhook event.
468	
469	### Key differences from manual-trigger debug
470	
471	| Aspect | Manual trigger | Connector trigger (polling) |
472	|---|---|---|
473	| Execution start | Immediate with user-provided inputs | Immediate with most recent matching event |
474	| User action needed | Provide input values | Ensure a matching event exists in the past ~1 hour |
475	| Failure mode | Missing required inputs | No matching events in lookback window (error 3005) |
476	
477	### Pre-debug checklist
478	
479	1. **Verify the connection is healthy** — `uip is connections ping "<id>"`
480	2. **Confirm a matching event exists** — the user should have produced the event (e.g., sent an email, created a Jira issue) within the past hour
481	3. **Check event mode** — if `webhooks`, debug is not supported; inform the user
482

484	
485	## Debug
486	
487	### Common Errors
488	
489	| Error | Cause | Fix |
490	|---|---|---|
491	| `Trigger nodes require --connection-id` | Ran `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id <id>` — required for all trigger nodes |
492	| `Invalid --detail` saying `objectName is required for the trigger` — or, on older CLIs, an opaque `Error configuring node` / `Response returned an error code` on every `--detail` shape | The trigger is **generic** (`activityType: "GenericTrigger"`, e.g. Data Fabric `record-created`): its manifest ships the `objectName` context entry without a value, and configure needs the object to fetch trigger metadata. Older CLIs rejected `objectName` as a `--detail` key and called the metadata API with an empty object name — hence the opaque server error. | Pass the object in `--detail.objectName` (resolve it per Step 1b-2). On an older CLI that rejects the key, `Edit` the trigger **definition's** `model.context` `objectName` entry to add `"value": "<object>"`, then re-run `node configure`. Curated triggers never need this — their manifest carries the objectName. |
493	| No trigger nodes in registry | Not authenticated or registry not pulled | Run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
494	| Connection not found in bindings | `node configure` not run or connection expired | Re-run `node configure` with valid `connectionId` and `folderKey` |
495	| Event parameter missing at runtime | Required event parameter not configured (commonly one returned by `triggers describe` but absent from `triggers objects → parameters[]`) | Re-run **both** `uip is triggers objects` (Step 1b) **and** `uip is triggers describe` (Step 1b-2). Configure every field marked `required` in **either** `parameters[]` or `EventParameters` (resolving references) under the correct `--detail` bucket. |
496	| `filterExpression is derived from the filter tree and cannot be provided directly` | Passed `filterExpression` string instead of a `filter` tree | Build a structured `filter` tree — see [Filter Trees](#filter-trees) |
497	| `Filter references field '<name>' which is not present in trigger metadata` | Leaf `id` does not match any `filterFields.fields[].name` | Re-run `registry get` and use a valid field name |
498	| Trigger not firing | Event parameters point to wrong resource (e.g., wrong folder ID) | Re-resolve reference fields with `uip is resources run list` |
499	| Trigger faults immediately with no visible error after a clean build | Event parameter uses a reference ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a `parentFolderId` for mailbox A pasted into a trigger bound to mailbox B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `eventParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 3 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
500	| Definition's `model.context` missing operation | Definition not copied correctly, or node added before registry pull | Re-run `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`, then verify the `definitions[]` entry contains `model.context` with `connectorKey`/`operation`/`objectName` as returned by `registry get` |
501	| Trigger faults at runtime with webhook-related error | Standard (non-BYOA) connection used for a trigger that requires `byoaConnection: true` | Run `uip is triggers objects` (Step 1b) to check `byoaConnection` flag, then switch to a BYOA connection with `uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --output json`. If no BYOA connections exist, user must create one. |
502	| `connections list` returns empty but connections exist in the IS portal | CLI is using cached connection data that is stale | Retry with `--refresh` flag: `uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --refresh --output json` |
503	| `ElementInstanceId` is empty on the selected connection | Connection is not a BYOA connection, or connector does not support webhooks on this connection type | Verify the trigger requires BYOA (Step 1b `byoaConnection` flag). If `true`, switch to a BYOA connection. |
504	
505	### Debug Tips
506	
507	1. **Always verify the connection is healthy** before debugging trigger issues — run `uip is connections ping "<id>"`
508	2. **`flow validate` does NOT catch trigger-specific issues** — missing event parameters, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime
509	3. **Event parameters with `reference` objects** need resolved IDs, not display names — same as IS activity fields
510	4. **Filters are optional** — omit `filter` from `--detail` if the user wants all events to trigger the flow. Do not invent an "empty" expression.
511	5. **Bindings are auto-managed** — `node configure` creates flow-level bindings; `flow debug`/packaging generates `bindings_v2.json` from them
512	6. **Use `uip maestro flow node remove` to remove the manual trigger** — do NOT use `Edit` to delete the start node. The CLI automatically removes associated edges, orphaned definitions, and regenerates `variables.nodes`. Hand-editing skips these cleanup steps and can leave orphaned references.
513	7. **Check `outputResponseDefinition` before writing downstream expressions** — trigger output field names vary by connector. Do not assume field names like `.text` or `.subject` — verify from the enriched `registry get` response (Step 2)
514	8. **Validate filter field names against `filterFields`** — only field names returned in `filterFields.fields[].name` are valid leaf `id`s in the filter tree. The CLI rejects trees that reference unknown fields at configure time, so guessing will surface as an `InvalidDetailError` rather than a silent runtime no-match.

If you landed here while adding/removing/wiring OOTB nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, or other structural graph elements, go back to the Edit / Write guide.

11	## Primitive Commands for Carve-Out Workflows
12	
13	### Add a node
14	
15	```bash
16	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <node-type> --output json \
17	  --input '<INPUT_JSON>' \
18	  --label "<LABEL>" \
19	  --position <X>,<Y>
20	```
21	
22	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
23	- Inserts node into `nodes` array with a generated `id`
24	- Copies the definition from the local registry cache into `definitions` (one per unique type)
25	- Adds node output variables to `variables.nodes`
26	
27	**Flags:**
28	
29	| Flag | Required | Description |
30	|------|----------|-------------|
31	| `--input` | No | JSON object of node-specific inputs (expression, script, URL, etc.). Omit for nodes with no inputs (merge, end, terminate). |
32	| `--label` | No | Display label shown on the canvas |
33	| `--position` | No | `x,y` coordinates. Any value is fine (e.g. `0,0`) — `flow format` rewrites positions on save. |
34	| `--output json` | Yes (for parsing) | Structured JSON response with the assigned node `id` |
35	
36	**Shell quoting tip:** If `--input` JSON contains special characters (quotes, braces, `$vars`), write it to a temp file and pass `--input "$(cat /tmp/input.json)"`.
37	
38	### Remove a node
39	
40	```bash
41	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID>
42	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> --output json
43	```
44	
45	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
46	- Removes the node from `nodes`
